Q: NPM publish to scoped private package without having to login A:

I think to publish your private npm-package you need to login to npm once for the first time. After the first successful login, the npm creates a _authToken in your .npmrc file. Until and unless your .npmrc file contains this _authToken with the appropriate value, you don't need to login again to npm to publish next npm-package.

Best of my knowledge, Unless you remove that _authToken Or delete the .npmrc file Or manually logged out from npm I am sure you don't have to login again to publish npm package.

Q: How can I use a single value from a string array as a record key? A:

A couple of helpful points have already been mentioned in the comments, so I'll summarize them here and add a bit more detail.

If your intent is to allow any search category to be provided, you can define it as below, as others suggested:

Record<T, any[]>

However If you want to allow only the selected categories `T`, you can probably do thate following:

Pick<Record<T, any[]>, T>

Check working snippet here.

You can enforce provide providing all categories like CategorySeaOrchResult<SearchCategory> instead of manually unioning all categories, which becomes handy in some situations.

I'll leave it upto you to decide whether the thing you're trying to do is best for your business use case.

Q: NextJS 14 (with electron) trying to use a .node addon - module not found A:

Instead of just addon.node, try:

const addonPath = path.join(process.cwd(), 'lib', 'my-addon.node');

If you want to do some verification, you can show it on console like:

console.log("Addon Path:", addonPath)

Q: Why are .fsx scripts executed when a compiled program is started? A:

It's a feature. The spec says "Side effects from all scripts are executed at program startup".
